name: β-Curcumene

pubchem.title: 1-(1,5-Dimethyl-4-hexen-1-yl)-4-methyl-1,4-cyclohexadiene
pubchem.description: Beta-curcumene is a sesquiterpene that is alpha-curcumene in which the p-tolyl group has been reduced to a 4-methylcyclohexa-1,4-dien-1-yl group. It is a sesquiterpene and a cyclohexadiene.

evidence: Measured in 4 of 6 MONDAYS hemp SKUs at 0.13–0.42% of total volatiles (0.026–0.084mg per chew).

consumer_summary.what_it_is: Beta-curcumene is a sesquiterpene, a type of aromatic molecule built by plants and microbes. It is closely related to the compounds that give turmeric its signature earthy scent. In daily life, you might encounter it in the essential oils of certain cypress trees or as a building block used by scientists to engineer complex fragrances.
consumer_summary.found_in: It is naturally found in the Nootka cypress, an evergreen tree native to the Pacific Northwest.
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are fascinated by beta-curcumene's role as a biological building block, particularly how bacteria and yeast can use it to synthesize highly valued fragrance compounds like ambrein. Beyond metabolic engineering, scientists are exploring its potential as an antimicrobial agent. The strongest evidence for its biological activity comes from human observational research (Oxford level 2b), which is prompting further investigation into how this molecule interacts with microbes.

structure_function.statement: Beta-curcumene may support the body's natural defenses against certain microbes.
structure_function.basis: This is based on four papers, including human observational research.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether beta-curcumene can actively inhibit the growth of problematic bacteria. If this bears out, it could serve as a natural template for new antibacterial agents or topical preservatives.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled human trial applying a standardized beta-curcumene topical formulation to superficial skin abrasions to measure bacterial load reduction and healing time over 14 days.

consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: Best evidence so far is human observational work (Oxford 2b) regarding its antimicrobial properties; most of the rest is biochemical research into its role in terpene synthesis.
